## Reproducibility and analytical choice {#one-number-the-whole-class}

:::: {.none}
::: {.fragment}
The class just got $\chi^2$ = `r fmt_num(chi_yates, 3)`, to the third decimal. That is reproducibility, and it is the easy R.
:::

::: {.fragment}
You all ran the *same code*. The five Multi100 analysts each wrote their own, on the same public file, and came back with five different numbers and two different verdicts.
:::

::: {.fragment}
None of them was careless. They made different choices, and the options that they chose from make up the **menu**.
:::
::::

::: notes
Look at what just happened. The whole class, on different machines, one number, agreeing to the third decimal. That is reproducibility, and notice how cheap it was: you all ran the same code on the same file, so of course you got the same number. Reproducibility is the easy R. [pause] Now set that against the five Multi100 analysts of this claim, whom we met earlier. They had the same public file, each wrote their own analysis, and they came back with five different numbers, and not even the same verdict on whether the data supported the claim. Not one of them was careless: four of the five published their scripts on the OSF, and they are competent pieces of work. So the spread is not a matter of quality. It is a matter of choices, and the menu is the full list of choices that were open to them.
:::
